label: Gets it right
quote: Every Halverson invoice since the MSA was countersigned on 2 Nov has been logged that way, even above $10k.
observed: Logged all 15 invoices correctly. It spotted the re-sent Vantor invoice, split Selbourne between Recruiting and People by size, noted card payments and read the contract exemption from the rows after November 2.
why: With enough recent examples, a strong agent can rebuild eight unwritten habits from a tracker alone. The habits are learnable.

label: Thin evidence
observed: Got 13 of 15 right, but flagged the $6,924 Marrow & Finch and $7,640 Selbourne invoices for review: with only three rows showing the new $10,000 cutoff, it kept the older $5,000 habit for them.
why: The same agent that is perfect at five examples misses a changed cutoff at three. Eight habits at once plus thin evidence is where the top models break.

label: Misses a newer habit
quote: VUM-2026-0497 marked DUPLICATE - do not pay
observed: Caught the duplicate and the reviewers, but left the Kellerby and Pellham invoices blank instead of noting "card", a habit that only started on October 19.
why: The most recent change, with the fewest rows behind it, is the one that slips. GPT-6.1 Sol made the same miss with the old policy doc in the drive.

label: Caution over precedent
quote: I didn't mark anything "PO matched". I couldn't check purchase orders, so the Infra invoices have no PO note.
observed: Read most habits correctly (reviewers, Recruiting split, duplicate, reclassified cost center) but refused to write the team's "PO matched" note because it could not verify a purchase order itself, and skipped the card notes.
why: This is a fair reading of an ambiguous note, and it is also why smaller models score low: they treat the team's conventions as claims to verify rather than habits to follow. Told the habit, Opus writes it every time.

label: Half follows the old doc
quote: Where the AP policy and the tracker disagree, I followed what the tracker does.
observed: Said it would follow the tracker over the policy, did so for cost centers, then still flagged every invoice over $5,000 for review, the January rule, including Halverson and the two mid-size invoices.
why: Stating the right principle and applying it everywhere are different things. Sonnet gets 0 of 15 tries fully right across levels at 5 examples, and 5 of 5 when told.

label: Not fooled by the old doc
observed: Logged all 15 invoices correctly with last year's AP policy in the drive, following the current quarter's rows wherever the policy was out of date.
why: A clearly dated policy is not a trap for the top models. The hard part is the number of habits and how many examples back each one.
